installed_attestation.scope: Read-only metadata and exact source/RECORD/dependency/cache proof. No Kernel/Store/workspace constructed, service state touched or actual loaded activation inferred. Supported owner/native proofs are separate.

module_paths.scope: Independent installed metadata subprocess with both private roots before imports, paired with supported actual loaded build/PID and native interpreter-path evidence. Not a claim that every installed module/branch executed in listener.

native.scope: Read-only exact native identity/class. No task policy, power, clock or service change.

fleet.scope: Required fields, not distinct incidents. One Macmini status field is stale with probe_failed, last attempt 319.3 ms. Fresh later fields do not resolve historical peer failures/build/log gaps. Correct last-attempt duration and nested static failure code now retained.

encoding.scope: Complete decoding/content length/schema and same-body parity; separate dynamic responses legitimately differ. Body bytes exclude headers and network framing; no decoded work or whole-path acceptance inferred.

validation.scope: Durable order, retained cold content hashes, projection head and card checks; includes awaited validation observer persistence. Excluded from workload duration and captured counters.

private_late.scope: Five independent private synthetic stores, 100,000 compatibility rows and 500 already-canonical selected rows each. Timed region is the unchanged native migration method only; seeding and assertions are outside. Small-sample quantiles, not production migration throughput, fresh health timing, statistical speedup or whole-PA acceptance. Both roots are private before PA imports; no live Store mutation or fault injection.

reference_guard.scope: Five alternating pairs per private synthetic population, identical 1000 distinct references with repeated retained events. Complete fresh reference sets and every event retained; a subsequent publication is visible to both methods. No object files are seeded or health file checks skipped by product code; this benchmark measures referenced_hashes only, not full health/maintenance or production load. SQL VM work is a separate instrumented pass excluded from latency samples. Source/archive methods differ only in type validation; no schema, policy, warning or deadline change. Small samples do not prove statistical whole-path speedup or deployed acceptance.

installed_lifecycle_links.scope: Thirty alternating pairs in one private synthetic store. Every status, realm and retired/terminal link is retained. Timers cover only the read, excluding comparison and observer persistence. Materialized JSON bytes are application copy work, not physical disk traffic. No provider closure, production workload, cadence/threshold change or whole-path speedup/acceptance is inferred. Both roots are private before PA imports.

installed_lifecycle_contracts.scope: Existing lifecycle obligation, retirement, closure and reserved-capacity/concurrency contracts against exact installed modules, both roots private before every PA import. No live closure/provider workload or whole-path performance acceptance.

natural_maintenance.scope: Supported owner GET of a cached snapshot. No new maintenance, GC, retention, backup or fault workload was invoked. Last-run phases are inclusive wall/thread-CPU spans; process maxima, phase durations and observer latency are distinct. Native busy/GIL/scheduling/physical IO remain unseparated.

failed_operations.scope: Last completed failed worker/native-async invocations and executor submission failures, including short failures. Worker caller timeouts/cancellations are not completion failures; their existing counters remain separate. Failed-only percentiles use the last 256 failures per operation and are omitted until a failure completes. Static categories are not root causes; no messages, arbitrary codes, exception names, arguments, SQL or payloads retained.

failed_requests.scope: Last completed HTTP 4xx/5xx responses, including failed SSE responses; normal SSE lifetimes remain excluded. Route templates and numeric status only, no response bodies, error codes, IDs or query strings.

source_matching_repair.cause: Every session filters all immutable watch links. A sweep-scoped index joins the same session-id OR nonempty-card-id keys while preserving original row order, distinct equal rows, retirement/status and the original early prompt/dispatch guards.

matching.scope: Private sparse-link comparison: five alternating actual decision sweeps, sparse immutable metadata links, candidate index construction included. No durable close, SQL, provider, service policy or PA store mutation. Does not measure the whole lifecycle sweep or establish historical cause. Uses the actual imported candidate index and actual decision method. Source or installed module path/hash is retained; the caller must distinguish these scopes.

source_matching_repair.tests: 91 passed / 22 subtests; index order/OR/duplicate/null-card parity, fresh worker construction and early prompt guard tested; prior 90-test stage retained.
source_matching_repair.implemented: Source only; protected ready PR, integration and exact activation/retests pending.
source_matching_repair.residual: Sparse-link comparison only, not whole sweep or historical cause. Worst-case shared-card matches remain; all-watch enumeration, session/dispatch/lease hydration/matching, lifecycle closure/concurrency/native contention and all maintenance/peer/log criteria remain open.

scope: Complete lossless installation bundle plus separate 85/22 and 85/34 runtime snapshots, all raw retest samples, CPU/SQL/lock/fsync/bytes/failure counters and initial/corrected source stages. Native full-prompt receipt and raw logs stay local/hash-only. Late migration overlapped private reference-guard preparation for about 0.279 s; fake starts overlapped that guard run. Public GET/Fleet/encoding windows and private mixed 100 were separate. Source comparison overlapped scoped regression tests; host load is uncontrolled, no isolated-host or causal claim. No prior artifact overwritten or distributions pooled.
